The address may be misspelled or may not exist. Try one or more of the following:

More Info for Email Admins	 
Status code: 550 5.1.1 

This error occurs because the sender sent a message to an email address outside of Office 365, but the address is incorrect or doesn't exist at the destination domain. The error is reported by the recipient domain's email server, but most often it must be fixed by the person who sent the message. If the steps in the How to Fix It section above don't fix the problem, and you're the email admin for the recipient, try one or more of the following:

The email address exists and is correct - Confirm that the recipient address exists, is correct, and is accepting messages.

Synchronize your directories - If you have a hybrid environment and are using directory synchronization make sure the recipient's email address is synced correctly in both Office 365 and in your on-premises directory.

Errant forwarding rule - Check for forwarding rules that aren't behaving as expected. Forwarding can be set up by an admin via mail flow rules or mailbox forwarding address settings, or by the recipient via the Inbox Rules feature.

Mail flow settings and MX records are not correct - Misconfigured mail flow or MX record settings can cause this error. Check your Office 365 mail flow settings to make sure your domain and any mail flow connectors are set up correctly. Also, work with your domain registrar to make sure the MX records for your domain are configured correctly.

For more information and additional tips to fix this issue, see Fix email delivery issues for error code 550 5.1.1 in Office 365 <https://na01.safelinks.protection.outlook.com/?url=https%3A%2F%2Fgo.microsoft.com%2Ffwlink%2F%3FLinkId%3D389363&data=05%7C02%7CSBNHotelJoiners%40seabourn.com%7C3aaeaa60b0be4aca06cc08dd317f8c57%7C9e37b9e905de4906b089536f19689074%7C0%7C0%7C638721146056401358%7CUnknown%7CTWFpbGZsb3d8eyJFbXB0eU1hcGkiOnRydWUsIlYiOiIwLjAuMDAwMCIsIlAiOiJXaW4zMiIsIkFOIjoiTWFpbCIsIldUIjoyfQ%3D%3D%7C0%7C%7C%7C&sdata=pfGj5QRFTfp0RbUCRQZ9qeu1WG8VplIwSIbLfgLohlM%3D&reserved=0> .

	I wanted to take a moment to extend our sincere thanks on behalf of my Seabourn Onboarding team for the excellent service and support you have provided to our team and our Crew Members in this season.  My team has regularly shared to me how supportive and excellent you are with your thorough communication and support.  

	 

	We are truly grateful for you!  

	 

	Below are some comments and thanks on behalf of my team:

	 

	I would like to express my deepest appreciation for Candela Gorza and the Ushuaia Shipping – Crew Port Agency and all the hard work during this Antarctic season, which started in November 2024 and ended in March 2025.I am pleased to say that Candela and the corresponding agency she belongs, Ushuaia Shipping – Crew Port Agency, have diligently worked and successfully managed transfers, hotels, and the immigration process;  basically, everything related to the onboarding process of our Exp TMs on both Seabourn Venture and Pursuit. Moreover, They successfully and promptly handled last minute hotel and transfer requests, of course , the invaluable support they provided at any hour for the immigration process and other matters. This was one of the rare times when the time zone difference was barely felt. Additionally, They consistently worked beyond their scope, even taking the time to understand the travel procedure of Seabourn with great diligence. They promptly and effectively take action in lastminute issues, demonstrating an excellent ability to adapt and learn our Company’s operational procedure in a very short time. In conclusion, I can sincerely say that this Port Agency, especially the port agent, Candela Gorza, never left our Team members alone for a single moment, whether during their journey from entering Argentina to join Seabourn Vessel or from their disembarkation until they left Argentina. Whenever there were uncertainties regarding flights, immigration, hotels, or transfers, they promptly contacted the right people between Crew Hotel- Crew Travel Team – Onboarding coordinators, raised the right concerns, and at the end resolved issues in the most effective, immediate, and optimal manner. I can only be grateful for the opportunity to have worked with this port agency and with Candela, who made this season, filled with endless flight changes, charter cancellations, and last minute Team member adjustments as smooth as possible. 

	 

	*******

	 

	Dear Candela, thank you so much for your constant help!

	You are  a blessing to work with, always supportive, professional, effective and positive.

	You are our hero girl from so called “End of the world” port😃 ❤

	All the best,

	 

	Stephanie

Your current scheduling has you set to join in the rank of CDC on the Seabourn Encore joining in Singapore, Singapore on 12/8/2024.

Good day all,

Please note we have several upcoming changes to transportation providers in contracted cities.
With these changes come the updated hotel letters to reflect new contact information for emergency purposes if transportation issues arise.
Attached you will find the updated hotel letters. Below you will find a list of dates the new transfer vendor goes into effect.
These letters have also been updated via the TP Central Teams page under Onboarding and Travel for GTP access.
If you have any questions or futher comments please reach out to me directly.


1.	


1.	
	Los Angeles - Effective 21DEC24 - Gold Coach Tours - 1-866-462-8737/ships@goldcoachtours.com
2.	
	San Diego - Effective 21DEC24 - Gold Coach Tours- 1-866-462-8737/ships@goldcoachtours.com
3.	
	San Francisco - Effective 24FEB25 - AAA Worldwide Transportation - 973-400-3200 Ext. 1215/zricks@lerostg.com; groups@royalcoachman.com
4.	
	New York - Effective 20JAN25 - SMS International Shore OPs - 305-290-3000/sam@sms.com.mt
5.	
	Vancouver - Effective 06JAN25 - Crewlink - 587-355-5827/ismail@crewslink.com
6.	
	Seattle - Effective 06JAN25 - AAA Worldwide Transportation - 973-400-3200 Ext. 1215/zricks@lerostg.com; groups@royalcoachman.com







Best Regards,




Jessica Bullough

Company Travel Supervisor | Travel Services

Holland America Group | Serving Princess Cruises, Holland America Line, Seabourn, and P&O Australia

24Hr Emergency Line: 1-877-558-2739 | jbullough@princesscruises.com

 

My hours are 6:00 a.m. – 03:45 p.m. and my 9/80 day off is Friday ( non-payday week)

Good day All

Please be advised that we wanted to send over update with regards to the standard subject lines.  Due to the Crew Planning team implementing their general inboxes, we have updated our subject line requests to include the Rank.  This allows for the proper routing for the Crew Planning teams general inboxes, as well as the crew travel teams inboxes.

We are now upon the high-volume season, with the holidays coming soon and we are seeing quite an influx of emails being sent in for many requests to be processed, without using the proper subject lines.  This will only delay our response as they may not get routed properly.  

I appreciate the urgency of needing the flights quickly when they are submitted into MAPS, we do our best to get the flights updated within 24 to 48 hours.  Keep this in mind before sending an email, as you may see the flights updated in MAPS, you can save yourself as well as the crew travel teams time by fielding an extra email.

Thank you very much for your assistance with this very important matter.

As always, if you have any questions or concerns, please feel free to reach out to me directly.

Regards
Nichole


Nichole Shelton 

Manager, Company Travel | Travel Services 

Serving Princess Cruises, Holland America Line, Seabourn, and P&O Australia 

24305 Town Center Drive | Santa Clarita, CA 91355

nshelton@hagroup.com <mailto:nshelton@hagroup.com>

Sent: Friday, January 20, 2023 3:32 PM
To: Shelton, Nichole (PCL) <nshelton@hagroup.com>; 
Subject: All Brands - Crew travel standard subject lines Template
 

Good day

 

In an effort to streamline the current high volume of emails and allow for faster response times, we have revised our current Email Template guide based on feedback and current trends we are experiencing.  By following the specific subject lines, this allows for smoother distribution of emails, so we can align our assignments properly to provide a quicker response to the current volume demand that we are experiencing.

 

We appreciate your assistance with these matters, and your patience while we continue to work through these requests.

 

If you should have any questions, please feel free to reach out to me directly.

 

Many thanks

Nichole

 



Nichole Shelton

		External Email: Be CAUTIOUS, particularly with links and attachments. DO NOT provide your username or password unless you expected this email or confirmed it separately. If you suspect that you have received a malicious email, click on "Submit a Phish" button.

________________________________

		 

		Good day Crew Care Team, 

		 

		I am writing in reference to the report key: 718044272301: regarding my unfair dismissal on July 22nd just shy of my sign-off date which was due to be August 16th.

		 

		The sequence of the events which led up to me getting an SD 6 and my subsequent discharge from the ship had started with me getting an SD1 (a written warning) for such a minor indiscretion not too long into my contract. This affected my confidence and self-esteem - especially because it was issued to me by my supervisor (Lauren Louise Lee) who I had been working with for 2 consecutive contracts. Since the first contract I worked with her on the Venture last year - she has been someone who tries to assert her authority through direct and indirect micro-aggressive racial stereotypical actions and statements. Since I was observant of that behaviour in her - she made it a point to victimize me in subtle ways; by always finding ways to criticise my work despite my best efforts.

		 

		Thereafter, there was an honest mistake I made which warranted a warning but again the Hotel Director - Nic Botha-Simpson issued me an SD4 - which I considered harsh but I accepted it as it was my own mistake.

		 

		Following up to this I made another minor transgression which led to me being issued an SD6. Chief Purser (Jo Marie van Biljon) made it a point to exaggerate the issue and prompted HRM Barry to summon a Masters hearing for me.

		 

		Throughout all these events I was subtly victimized, told that I was being put on a PIP (Performance Improvement Plan) which caused me emotional distress and subsequently affected my work performance as I was made to feel like an incompetent team member.

		 

		No one in the so-called management would take notice of all the other areas that I thrived in - I had frequent positive guest recognition and feedback; but when mistakes happened - that was highlighted as if all my other best efforts meant nothing.

		 

		As I type up this email, I am back home in South Africa - jobless and stressed out for my family and I. It took me time to muster up the courage to even send this email as I have been processing this whole situation. 

		 

		I know that I made my mistakes but an equally mean-spirited management (mainly comprising of Caucasian South Africans - notorious for racism) created a toxic working environment that affected not only myself  but other crew members. Perhaps their cases were not as extreme that is why there may be no mention of them.

		 

		The above-mentioned Officers lack empathy, compassion and rather invalidate team members despite their best efforts. They unfairly enforce policies as a way to assert their authority. My dismissal was a few days before the start of a new cruise which meant that the team ended up having a short staffed cruise for the Guest Services department.They were so eager to get rid of me like I was the worst thing -  they didn't  even consider how that would affect operations - that's how irrational they are. 

		 

		Sincerely,

		Lorraine Munashe Mudede

		082 752 3298
